authors: Veronica Romano, Davide De Biase, Valeria Russo, Evaristo Di Napoli, Orlando Paciello, Giuseppe Piegari

mcqs.q: Why is fatal non-drowning asphyxia one of the hardest forensic diagnoses to confirm at necropsy?
o: It produces florid pathognomonic lesions that confuse examiners
Gross findings are subtle, non-specific, and easily masked by postmortem change
It always requires toxicology that is rarely available
Asphyxial deaths leave no histological changes at all
mcqs.e: The review stresses asphyxia yields only subtle, non-pathognomonic gross signs readily obscured by postmortem alterations.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT one of the asphyxia categories described in the review?
mcqs.e: The categories given are strangulation, suffocation, mechanical asphyxia, and drowning; anaphylaxis is not listed.

mcqs.q: What does reliable diagnosis of asphyxiation depend on?
o: Integrating scene context, history, and ancillary histology/biomarkers rather than gross necropsy alone
Excluding all other causes by toxicology only
mcqs.e: Because gross signs are non-specific, diagnosis requires synthesizing history, scene analysis, and ancillary tests.

authors: Apichaya Lorsirigool, Yutthana Sudjaroen, Nuttapon Kulnides, Natapol Pumipuntu, Atthaporn Roongsitthichai, Supawadee Piratae, Maluna Intrakamhaeng, Sirintip Chaiyasak, Kanokwan Saenkaew

mcqs.q: According to the veterinarians surveyed, what most limited effective enforcement of existing anti-cruelty law?
o: Absence of standardized forensic protocols, limited training, and restricted inspection authority
mcqs.e: Investigative challenges were driven by missing forensic protocols, limited forensic training, and restricted inspection authority.

mcqs.q: Within which framework did respondents situate strengthening cruelty-investigation capacity?
mcqs.e: The study frames harmonized forensic protocols and coordinated enforcement under a One Welfare model.

mcqs.q: How did most respondents view the current animal-cruelty legislation?
o: Partially effective but with critical gaps
mcqs.e: Most perceived the law as partially effective, citing ambiguous definitions, inconsistent enforcement, and limited public awareness.

authors: Reina Ueda, Yuko Kihara, Aki Tanaka

mcqs.q: What was novel about this dog-bite identification case?
o: A full canine STR profile was recovered from trace DNA on clothing with no visible blood or saliva
The dog was identified solely by bite-mark morphology
Mitochondrial DNA alone identified the dog
Identification required a fresh saliva swab from the wound
mcqs.e: STR analysis of invisible trace DNA on clothing yielded a complete profile, a first for samples lacking visible traces.

mcqs.q: How completely did the recovered STR profile match the offending Weimaraner?
o: Partial match at a few loci
Complete match at all 19 loci examined
Match only by exclusion of other breeds
mcqs.e: The profile matched one of three suspected dogs at all 19 loci.

mcqs.q: What did the authors say is needed to advance canine DNA forensics?
o: Accumulating allele-frequency data and standardizing analytical procedures
mcqs.e: They underscore building population allele-frequency databases and standardizing methods.

authors: Parshant Dahiya, Ashna Bhatia, Sahil Khatri
journal: Perspectives in Legal and Forensic Sciences

mcqs.q: What chiefly limits the reliability of the diatom test for diagnosing drowning?
o: It is too expensive for routine use
It only works in saltwater drowning
mcqs.e: The review notes the diatom test is undermined by environmental contamination and non-standardized protocols.

mcqs.q: How does the review characterize classic findings like pulmonary edema and frothy exudate?
mcqs.e: These signs are described as frequently non-specific and not confirmatory.

mcqs.q: What approach does the review propose for diagnosing drowning?
o: Rely on a single pathognomonic lesion
Use the diatom test in isolation
An integrated approach combining scene, gross, histology, and ancillary tests
Diagnose by exclusion of toxicology alone
mcqs.e: Because no single finding is reliable, an integrated diagnostic strategy is recommended.

authors: Quintana J, Viola L, Sanchez V, Scott D, Duncan C

mcqs.q: How did pet owners regard veterinary teams as a source of disaster-preparedness information?
o: As trustworthy sources whose support they would welcome
As only useful for medical emergencies
mcqs.e: Owners overwhelmingly viewed pet-health professionals as trustworthy and wanted their help building pet-inclusive plans.

mcqs.q: What did the surveys reveal about disaster preparedness during routine vet visits?
o: It is the topic most often discussed
It is rarely covered, leaving an actionable gap
Staff are forbidden from raising it
mcqs.e: Both groups reported the topic was not typically covered, an opportunity to integrate into practice.

authors: Chapman AJ, Bennett PC, Rohlf VI

mcqs.q: Before selecting burnout-reduction strategies, what did the experts say must happen first?
o: Evaluate existing workplace barriers to maximize strategy effectiveness
mcqs.e: The study concludes workplace barriers must be evaluated before choosing context-appropriate strategies.

mcqs.q: Which themes characterized the most highly rated solutions?
o: Improved communication, progression pathways, and leadership training/support
mcqs.e: Top-rated solutions centered on communication, career progression, and leadership support.

mcqs.q: Which method was used to develop the expert recommendations?
mcqs.e: The study used a two-round Delphi method with experienced experts.

authors: Moslehi S, Tavan A, Narimani S, Soleimanpour S

mcqs.q: Which psychological frameworks did the scoping review highlight for improving pet disaster outcomes?
o: Trans-theoretical Model and Protection Motivation Theory
Health Belief Model and Five Freedoms
mcqs.e: The conclusions center on the Trans-theoretical Model and Protection Motivation Theory to drive owner preparedness.

mcqs.q: What gap in current disaster programs did the review identify?
o: They overemphasize pets at the expense of people
They focus on human populations and overlook pets
mcqs.e: Most disaster programs target humans and overlook the role of pets during emergencies.

authors: Kathleen A Cooney, Sheilah A Robertson, Lori R Kogan

mcqs.q: Under what essential condition did lidocaine and mepivacaine reliably cause death in this study?
mcqs.e: Death was achieved at lethal doses but only following induction of general anesthesia.

mcqs.q: How did the intrathecal route compare with IV or intracardiac administration?
o: Faster to death with more active signs of dying
Slower to cardiac standstill but with reduced active signs of dying
Faster and with no signs of dying
mcqs.e: Intrathecal took longer to reach cardiac standstill but showed fewer active signs of death.

mcqs.q: What is the clinical relevance of these findings?
o: They are alternative euthanasia agents when pentobarbital is unavailable or undesired
They are first-line over pentobarbital in all cases
They work without any dosing limits
mcqs.e: The agents are positioned as alternatives when pentobarbital sodium is unavailable or undesired.

journal: Journal of Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care

mcqs.q: How does RECOVER newborn resuscitation differ from adult CPR?
o: It is compression-centric like adult CPR
It is respiration-centric, starting with airway clearance, tactile stimulation, temperature control, then ventilation
mcqs.e: Newborn resuscitation prioritizes airway, stimulation, warmth, and positive-pressure ventilation rather than chest compressions first.

mcqs.q: What did the RECOVER newborn guidelines provide to standardize the resuscitation process?
o: A single fixed drug dose with no assessment steps
An algorithm displaying the flow of assessments and actions, plus 59 treatment recommendations developed from 28 PICO questions
Recommendations for puppies only, excluding kittens
mcqs.e: The project addressed 28 PICO questions and produced 59 treatment recommendations plus an algorithm displaying the flow of assessments and actions for newborn puppies and kittens.

mcqs.q: Which welfare issue was rated most impactful across most pet small-mammal species?
mcqs.e: Undersized housing scored highest for impact in all species except the rat.

mcqs.q: For which species was respiratory disease the top welfare concern?
mcqs.e: Respiratory disease was the leading concern specifically for rats.

mcqs.q: How did veterinary nurses' ratings differ from veterinary surgeons'?
o: Nurses rated issues as less prevalent
Nurses generally rated welfare issues as more prevalent
mcqs.e: Veterinary nurses generally rated welfare issues as more prevalent than surgeons.

mcqs.q: Which lidocaine technique was recommended as first choice for feline castration analgesia?
mcqs.e: The intratesticular block gave more stable intraoperative vitals and less postoperative pain.

mcqs.q: When is spermatic cord instillation a useful alternative?
o: When testicular masses or infection preclude intratesticular injection
mcqs.e: Instillation is the fallback when testicular pathology limits intratesticular injection.

authors: Jacob Aiello, Brittney Carson, Turi Aarnes, Audrey Wanstrath, Mary McLoughlin

mcqs.q: What effect did oral gabapentin (20 mg/kg) plus trazodone (8 mg/kg) have on isoflurane requirements?
o: A MAC-sparing effect, reducing isoflurane MAC by roughly one-third
mcqs.e: MAC fell from 0.95% to 0.625%, about a 34% reduction.

mcqs.q: What was the hemodynamic impact of the premedication?
o: Heart rate decreased but stayed within normal limits, with no significant hemodynamic compromise
mcqs.e: Heart rate decreased but remained normal, and other hemodynamic variables did not differ significantly.
